title: Print Zero Even Odd
statement:
On LeetCode this is a multithreading problem. Here each thread is an asynchronous task, and you coordinate the tasks with promises.

Write a class `ZeroEvenOdd` whose constructor takes `n`. One shared instance is handed to three threads: one calls `zero(printNumber)`, one calls `even(printNumber)` and one calls `odd(printNumber)`. Calling `printNumber(x)` prints the integer `x`. Between them the three methods must print `0, 1, 0, 2, 0, 3, ..., 0, n`: every number from 1 to `n` in increasing order, each preceded by a 0, so `2n` prints that read `"010203..."` when joined. `zero` prints only the zeros (all `n` of them), `even` only the even numbers of 1..n and `odd` only the odd ones. Each method keeps going until its whole share is printed, so make the methods `async` and `await` promises between prints.

Each case gives `n`, `threads` and `starts`: thread `i` starts at `starts[i]` ms and calls the method named `threads[i]`. Threads with the same start time start in index order. The answer is `{ output, times }`: everything printed, joined into one string, and the time in ms of each print, in the order the prints happened. A number must be printed as soon as it is allowed, that is, once its thread has started and the print before it has happened, so wait on promises rather than on timers.
signature: Object ZeroEvenOdd(int n, String[] threads, int[] starts)
api: class ZeroEvenOdd { constructor(n: number); zero(printNumber: (x: number) => void): void | Promise<void>; even(printNumber: (x: number) => void): void | Promise<void>; odd(printNumber: (x: number) => void): void | Promise<void> }
notes:
## Intuition

The three threads take turns, and the next turn is always known: after a zero comes the next number, odd or even depending on its parity, and after any number comes a zero. So keep one piece of shared state, `turn`, naming whose go it is. A method whose turn has not come parks: it stores the resolve function of a fresh promise and awaits it. Handing over the turn resolves that promise, which wakes exactly the right thread. (The brute force instead lets whichever thread arrives last print every position whose owner has already arrived.)

## Approach

1. Start with `turn = 'zero'` and an empty `parked` map.
2. `waitTurn(name)` returns a resolved promise if it is already `name`'s turn; otherwise it parks `name` by storing the resolve function with `parked.set(name, resolve)`.
3. `giveTurn(name)` sets `turn`, takes `parked.get(name)`, removes the entry with `parked.delete(name)` and calls the resolve function if that thread was waiting.
4. `zero` loops `i` from 1 to `n`: wait, print 0, then give the turn to `odd` if `i` is odd, else to `even`.
5. `even` and `odd` loop over their own numbers: wait, print `i`, give the turn back to `zero`.

With real threads the same design uses three semaphores: `zeroSem` starts at 1, `oddSem` and `evenSem` at 0. Each method acquires its own semaphore before printing and releases the next one afterwards. Or one lock with a condition variable: wait while `turn` is not yours, print, set `turn`, `notifyAll`. Awaiting a parked promise plays the part of acquire or wait, and calling its resolve function the part of release or notify.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 2`; threads start in the order zero, even, odd at 0 ms.

- `zero` has the turn: it prints 0, gives the turn to `odd`, then parks.
- `even` arrives and parks; `odd` arrives, finds its turn, prints 1 and wakes `zero`.
- `zero` prints 0 and wakes `even`, which prints 2. The answer is `{ output: "0102", times: [0, 0, 0, 0] }`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): 2n prints, each with O(1) handoff work.
- Space: O(1): the turn and at most three parked resolve functions.

## Pitfalls

- The first odd number follows the first zero; giving the turn to `even` when `i` is odd prints numbers out of order.
- Printing before waiting: every print, including the first zero, must check the turn.
- Polling a flag with `setTimeout` prints late; wait on the promise itself.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `turn` | which method may print next: `'zero'`, `'odd'` or `'even'` |
| `parked` | map from the name of each thread that is waiting for its turn to its resolve function |
| `i` | the loop counter: a zero's index in `zero`, the number to print in `even` and `odd` |
| `wake` | the resolve function that `giveTurn` calls, if that thread is waiting |
